Nanchang Urban Rail Group Co..desc: A Nanchang city state-owned company registered as 南昌轨道交通集团有限公司 (Nanchang Rail Transit Group Co., Ltd. in translation; the filing gives no English name). A 2019 bond-disclosure credit rating report describes it as the body that carries out Nanchang's rail transit investment, construction and operation, with a business scope covering project investment, construction, engineering consultancy and design, rail operation, rail communications and other franchised operations, and names the Nanchang municipal state-asset supervision commission as its actual controller, holding 100 per cent. At the end of March 2019 its registered and paid-in capital were both 26.15亿元 (RMB 2.615 billion) and consolidated total assets were 724.95亿元 (RMB 72.495 billion).

sources.title: Follow-up credit rating report on 南昌轨道交通集团有限公司, corporate bond disclosure
sources.publisher: 联合资信, filed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange disclosure server

State Council Leading Group Office for P.desc: A Chinese central government office, 国务院扶贫开发领导小组办公室, set up in 1986. Xinhua reported that its sign had been permanently taken down and that at 16:00 on 25 February 2021 the sign of the newly established National Administration for Rural Revitalization was hung at No. 1 Taiyanggong North Street, Chaoyang District, Beijing, the 1986 office's "historical mission" having ended. The report does not say what the office did.

sources.title: 国家乡村振兴局正式挂牌

Open Shareholding Holding Company Barki.desc: Tajikistan's state power group. Its audited consolidated accounts for 2018 give the legal name as Open Joint Stock Holding Company "Barqi Tojik", registered with Tajikistan's Ministry of Justice on 3 June 1999, with the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan as sole shareholder; the principal activity is generation, transmission and distribution of electricity and thermal energy, electricity being generated at five hydropower stations that are structural units of the group, and it had 11,230 employees at 31 December 2018. The same accounts record Government Decree No. 234 of 28 April 2018, under which ten of its subsidiaries were to be merged into new joint-stock companies for transmission grids and for distribution grids, an effect management said it could not yet assess.

sources.title: Barki Tajik entity audit report for the year ended December 31, 2018 — audited consolidated financial statements, Notes 1 and 2

Accra Metropolitan Assembly.desc: The metropolitan district assembly for Accra, Ghana. Its own pages give its legal basis as the Local Government Act, 1993 (Act 462), since amended as the Local Governance Act, 2016 (Act 936) — section 12(3) of which the Assembly describes as establishing it and setting its functions, among them responsibility for the overall development of the district — together with Legislative Instrument 2034. Its General Assembly has 34 members: 20 elected, 10 government appointees, 3 members of parliament and the Metro Chief Executive, who chairs the Executive Committee; ten Sub-Metropolitan District Councils are subordinate bodies of the Assembly, and 14 sub-committees make recommendations to the Executive Committee.

Ministry of Local Government and Rural D.desc: Ghana's central ministry for local government, under the name the project documents use. The ministry of that name no longer exists: the successor ministry's Medium Term Development Plan 2026-2029 records that Executive Instrument 1, enacted in January 2025, established the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs out of the former Ministry of Local Government, Decentralisation and Rural Development, the Ministry of Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs and the sanitation ministry — which the plan names in one place as the Ministry of Sanitation and in another as the Ministry of Sanitation and Water Resources. The successor's mandate covers decentralisation policy, local governance, rural and urban development, environmental health and sanitation, and chieftaincy and religious affairs, and the plan refers to 261 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies.

sources.title: Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Medium Term Development Plan 2026-2029

Direccion Provincial de Vialidad, Provin.desc: The provincial roads directorate of Santa Fe, Argentina, at Boulevard Muttis 880 in the city of Santa Fe, with its own Dirección General de Proyectos at the same address. It opens and receives bids for works on provincial routes — a 2025 provincial tender for repaving on Provincial Routes 2 and 5 names the Ministerio de Obras Públicas as the organismo and the directorate as the place of bid opening. In the province's 2009 investment programming it is budget entity 601, "Vialidad", under jurisdiction 62, "MOP y Vivienda", and is listed as the executing unit for its own works; neither document states that the directorate sits under that ministry, and no creation law was found.

Direccion Nacional de Vialidad.desc: Argentina's national roads body, constituted as an autarchic entity by Decreto-Ley 505/58 and latterly within the Secretaría de Transporte of the Ministerio de Economía. Decree 461/2025, signed 7 July 2025 and effective on publication the following day, dissolved it (Article 1) and gave the study, construction, conservation and improvement of the national trunk road network to the Ministerio de Economía (Article 6), directing that references to the directorate in that decree-law be read as references to the ministry. The decree does not mention Ley 11.658 of 1932, the date usually given for the body's creation.

Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation.desc: A municipal corporation in the Indian state of Maharashtra, governed by the amended Maharashtra Municipal Corporation Act, 1949, which applies to every corporation in the state except Greater Mumbai. India's Comptroller and Auditor General, reporting for the year ended 31 March 2015, places it in Category B — corporations with a population between 15 and 25 lakh and per capita income above ₹5,000 — one of three in that category alongside Nashik and Thane.

sources.title: Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on Local Bodies, Government of Maharashtra, for the year ended 31 March 2015 — Chapter 3
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

Hubli-Dharwad Bus Rapid Transit System C.desc: A state government company in Karnataka, India, listed by India's Comptroller and Auditor General as "Hubli Dharwad BRTS Company Limited (HDBRTS)", a working government company in the infrastructure sector — a class the report defines, after section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013, as companies with at least 51 per cent of paid-up share capital held by government. Its latest accounts finalised at the time of that 2018 report were for 2015-16 and showed paid-up capital of ₹20 crore; the report lists it among the undertakings whose accounts were in arrears, with 2016-17 still pending. The report names no administrative department and no incorporation date.

Tanzania National Roads Agency.desc: A Tanzanian government executive agency whose roles the national audit office cites from Rule 3(3) of the Executive Agencies (The Tanzania National Roads Agency) (Amendment) Order No. 350 of 2009, and whose performance on road maintenance the Ministry of Works and Transport oversees. The Roads Act, 2007 requires it, as a roads authority, to prepare and implement short and long-term road maintenance programmes. The audit, citing the Roads Fund Board's annual report of June 2019, records it as maintaining a national network of 36,258 km — 12,176 km of trunk roads and 24,082 km of regional roads, of which 1,756 km were paved.

sources.title: Performance Audit Report on Maintenance of Roads
sources.publisher: Controller and Auditor General, United Republic of Tanzania

Kenya National Highways Authority.desc: A Kenyan state body established under the Kenya Roads Act, 2007 and, by its own account, inaugurated in September 2008. Its own page gives its remit as the development, rehabilitation, management and maintenance of all national trunk roads, which it defines as the Class S, A and B roads.

sources.title: Kenya National Highways Authority — Who we are

Kenya Urban Roads Authority.desc: A Kenyan state corporation established under the Kenya Roads Act, 2007. Its own site states its remit twice and not identically: under "Our Mandate" as the management, development, rehabilitation and maintenance of all national urban roads, and under "Who we are" as national trunk roads within urban areas. It puts that network at about 4,625 km, paved and unpaved.

sources.title: Kenya Urban Roads Authority — Who we are / Our Mandate

National Land Commission.desc: A Kenyan constitutional commission established under Article 67(1) of the 2010 Constitution and made operational by the National Land Commission Act, the Land Act and the Land Registration Act of 2012, its first commissioners gazetted on 20 February 2013 and beginning their term on 23 February. Its constitutional functions include managing public land on behalf of the national and county governments, recommending land policy, advising on title registration, investigating present and historical land injustices and recommending redress, assessing land taxes and premiums, and oversight of land use planning. Under Part VIII of the Land Act, 2012 it also handles compulsory acquisition: acquiring authorities submit requests to it (s. 107), it has the affected land mapped and valued, holds the inquiry into compensation claims (s. 112), prepares the written award of compensation (s. 113) and pays it from funds the acquiring authority deposits with it (ss. 111, 115).

sources.title: Land Act (Cap. 280, Act No. 6 of 2012), Part VIII, ss. 107, 111, 112, 113, 115, revised text

Tanzania Airports Authority.desc: A Tanzanian government executive agency established on 29 November 1999 by the Executive Agencies (Tanzania Airports Authority) (Establishment) Order, G.N. No. 404 of 1999, as an executive agency "in relation to the Department of Aerodromes". Its framework document gives its role as to "operate, manage, maintain and develop Government-owned airports in a professional and cost-effective manner", and names the Minister for Communications and Transport as the responsible minister.

Anhui Provincial Transport Department.desc: The transport department of the Anhui provincial government in China, 安徽省交通运输厅. A layout plan it issued in October 2022 for expressway traffic enforcement stations records that in 2003 the department, with the provincial office of establishment, applied the principle of separating government from enterprise and transferred the road-administration functions then carried by expressway operating companies to the former Provincial Highway Administration Bureau; it also records the department being tasked by the provincial government with selecting enforcement station sites together with expressway owners and supervising construction, and issuing a province-wide three-year plan for standardising comprehensive transport administrative enforcement.
